title: Prakrama 2, Sarga 11. The Plunge into the Jahnavi
html:
The brahmana Vanamali sees the boy Krishna; the Lord in the mood of Nrisimha; the Lord as Shiva on a singer's shoulders; a brahmana woman takes the dust of His feet, and the Lord throws Himself into the Ganga

Verse 1

भिक्षुः कश्चिद्वनमाली द्विजस्तत्र समागतः।
सपुत्रो देवदेवेशं ददर्श च ननर्त च॥१॥

bhikṣuḥ kaścidvanamālī dvijastatra samāgataḥ|
saputro devadeveśaṁ dadarśa ca nanarta ca||1||

bhikshuh — a mendicant; kashchit — certain; vanamali — Vanamali; dvijah — a brahmana; tatra — there; samagatah — came; sa-putrah — with his son; deva-deva-isham — the Lord of the god of gods; dadarsha — saw; cha — and; nanarta — danced; cha — and.

1Once a certain mendicant brahmana named Vanamali came there with his son; he saw the Lord of the god of gods and broke into dance.

Verse 2

तं दृष्ट्वा भगवान्प्रीत्या तेन सार्धं हरिं जगौ।
हरेः सोऽपि प्रसादेन सपुत्रो मुमुदे सुखम्॥२॥

taṁ dṛṣṭvā bhagavānprītyā tena sārdhaṁ hariṁ jagau|
hareḥ so'pi prasādena saputro mumude sukham||2||

tam — him; drishtva — seeing; bhagavan — Bhagavan; pritya — lovingly; tena — with him; sardham — together; harim — of Hari; jagau — sang; hareh — of Hari; sah — he; api — too; prasadena — by the grace; sa-putrah — with his son; mumude — rejoiced; sukham — happily.

2Seeing him, Bhagavan lovingly sang of Hari together with him; and he and his son rejoiced happily by the grace of Hari.

Verse 3

एकदा कीर्तनपरे हरौ नृत्यति स द्विजः।
ददर्श बालकं कञ्चिच्छ्यामं पीताम्बरावृतम्॥३॥

ekadā kīrtanapare harau nṛtyati sa dvijaḥ|
dadarśa bālakaṁ kañcicchyāmaṁ pītāmbarāvṛtam||3||

ekada — once; kirtana-pare — absorbed in kirtana; harau — while Hari; nrityati — is dancing; sah — that; dvijah — brahmana; dadarsha — saw; balakam — a boy; kanchit — certain; shyamam — dark; pita-ambara-avritam — clad in yellow garments.

3Once, while Hari was dancing, absorbed in kirtana, that brahmana saw a certain dark boy clad in yellow garments.

Verse 4

दृष्टो दृष्टो मया देव इति हृष्टो बभूव ह।
स जन्म सार्थकं मेने भिक्षुधर्मो द्विजोत्तमः॥४॥

dṛṣṭo dṛṣṭo mayā deva iti hṛṣṭo babhūva ha|
sa janma sārthakaṁ mene bhikṣudharmo dvijottamaḥ||4||

drishtah drishtah — seen, seen; maya — by me; devah — the Lord; iti — thus; hrishtah — jubilant; babhuva — became; ha — indeed; sah — that; janma — birth; sa-arthakam — fulfilled; mene — considered; bhikshu-dharmah — following the mendicant's way; dvija-uttamah — the best of brahmanas.

4"I have seen the Lord, I have seen Him!" he cried, jubilant; and that best of brahmanas, who lived as a mendicant, held that his birth had attained its purpose.

Verse 5

पुत्रं गृहीत्वा हस्ताभ्यामागतः प्रभुसन्निधिम्।
एवं भिक्षुः स हृष्टाङ्गः पुलकावलिमुद्वहन्॥५॥

putraṁ gṛhītvā hastābhyāmāgataḥ prabhusannidhim|
evaṁ bhikṣuḥ sa hṛṣṭāṅgaḥ pulakāvalimudvahan||5||

putram — his son; grihitva — taking; hastabhyam — by the hands; agatah — came; prabhu-sannidhim — into the Lord's presence; evam — thus; bhikshuh — the mendicant; sah — he; hrishta-angah — his body thrilled; pulaka-avalim — rows of bristling hair; udvahan — bearing.

5Taking his son by the hands, he came into the Lord's presence; and so the mendicant, his whole body thrilled, the hair of his body standing in rows,

Verse 6

प्रेमाश्रुधारासिक्ताङ्गो ननर्त सह चक्रिणा।
एकदा पैतृकं कर्म कृत्वा श्रीवासपण्डितः॥६॥

premāśrudhārāsiktāṅgo nanarta saha cakriṇā|
ekadā paitṛkaṁ karma kṛtvā śrīvāsapaṇḍitaḥ||6||

prema-ashru-dhara-sikta-angah — his body bathed in streams of tears of love; nanarta — danced; saha — together; chakrina — with the Holder of the discus; ekada — once; paitrikam — ancestral; karma — rite; kritva — having performed; shrivasa-panditah — Srivasa Pandita.

6bathed in streams of tears of love, danced together with the Holder of the discus. Once Srivasa Pandita, having performed the rite for his ancestors,

Verse 7

शृण्वन्बृहत्सहस्रं स नाम कृष्णस्य शुद्धधीः।
तत्राजगाम भगवाञ्छ्रुत्वा च हरिनामकम्॥७॥

śṛṇvanbṛhatsahasraṁ sa nāma kṛṣṇasya śuddhadhīḥ|
tatrājagāma bhagavāñchrutvā ca harināmakam||7||

shrinvan — listening to; brihat — the great; sahasram — thousand; sah — he; nama — names; krishnasya — of Krishna; shuddha-dhih — pure-minded; tatra — there; ajagama — came; bhagavan — Bhagavan; shrutva — hearing; cha — and; hari-namakam — the names of Hari.

7was listening, pure of mind, to the great Thousand Names of Krishna1; and Bhagavan came there, having heard the names of Hari.

Verse 8

नृसिंहावेशसंक्रुद्धो गदामादाय सत्वरः।
धावति स्म ततो देवो नृसिंहाकारविक्रमः॥८॥

nṛsiṁhāveśasaṁkruddho gadāmādāya satvaraḥ|
dhāvati sma tato devo nṛsiṁhākāravikramaḥ||8||

nrisimha-avesha-samkruddhah — enraged, possessed by the mood of Nrisimha; gadam — a club; adaya — seizing; satvarah — swiftly; dhavati sma — ran; tatah — then; devah — the Lord; nrisimha-akara-vikramah — with the form and might of Nrisimha.

8Possessed by the mood of Nrisimha2 and enraged, the Lord swiftly seized a club and ran, with the form and might of Nrisimha.

Verse 9

एवंभूतं च तं देवं दृष्ट्वा सर्वे प्रदुद्रुवुः।
पलायनपरान्दृष्ट्वा ततस्तान्नृहरिः पुनः॥९॥

evaṁbhūtaṁ ca taṁ devaṁ dṛṣṭvā sarve pradudruvuḥ|
palāyanaparāndṛṣṭvā tatastānnṛhariḥ punaḥ||9||

evam-bhutam — in such a state; cha — and; tam — that; devam — Lord; drishtva — seeing; sarve — all; pradudruvuh — fled; palayana-paran — intent on flight; drishtva — seeing; tatah — then; tan — them; nriharih — Nrihari; punah — in turn.

9Seeing the Lord in such a state, everyone fled. And Nrihari, seeing them take to flight,

Verse 10

क्षणाद्गदां परित्यज्य सुस्थ आविशदासने।
तदोवाच न जानेऽहमपराधः क्वचिन्मम॥१०॥

kṣaṇādgadāṁ parityajya sustha āviśadāsane|
tadovāca na jāne'hamaparādhaḥ kvacinmama||10||

kshanat — in a moment; gadam — the club; parityajya — throwing down; susthah — composed again; avishat — sat; asane — on the seat; tada — then; uvacha — said; na jane — do not know; aham — I; aparadhah — an offence; kvachit — any; mama — My.

10in a moment threw down the club, came back to Himself and sat down on His seat. Then He said: "I do not know whether I have committed some offence."

Verse 11

भवेदिति वचः श्रुत्वा सर्वे प्रोचुर्न ते क्वचित्।
अपराधो जगन्नाथ यद्दर्शनमनुस्मरन्॥११॥

bhavediti vacaḥ śrutvā sarve procurna te kvacit|
aparādho jagannātha yaddarśanamanusmaran||11||

bhavet — may have been; iti — thus; vachah — the words; shrutva — hearing; sarve — all; prochuh — said; na — not; te — of You; kvachit — any; aparadhah — offence; jagannatha — O Lord of the world; yat-darshanam — the sight of whom; anusmaran — one remembering.

11Hearing these words, all said: "You have no offence at all, O Lord of the world! Whoever only remembers having seen You,

Verse 12

पापबीजं दहेदेव नरसिंहाकृतेः प्रभोः।
अपराधस्तव भवेत्कदाचिदपि मानद॥१२॥

pāpabījaṁ dahedeva narasiṁhākṛteḥ prabhoḥ|
aparādhastava bhavetkadācidapi mānada||12||

papa-bijam — the seed of sin; dahet — would burn; eva — surely; narasimha-akriteh — in the form of Narasimha; prabhoh — of the Lord; aparadhah — an offence; tava — of Yours; bhavet — could there be; kadachit api — ever; manada — O Giver of honour.

12the Lord in the form of Narasimha — in him the very seed of sin is surely burnt away. How could You ever commit an offence, O Giver of honour?"

Verse 13

अथापरदिने कश्चिद्गायनः समुपागतः।
नमस्कृत्य हरिं भक्त्या तत्रोपविश्य भूतले॥१३॥

athāparadine kaścidgāyanaḥ samupāgataḥ|
namaskṛtya hariṁ bhaktyā tatropaviśya bhūtale||13||

atha — now; apara-dine — on another day; kashchit — a certain; gayanah — singer; samupagatah — came; namaskritya — having bowed; harim — to Hari; bhaktya — with devotion; tatra — there; upavishya — sitting down; bhu-tale — on the ground.

13Now on another day a certain singer came; having bowed to Hari with devotion, he sat down there on the ground

Verse 14

जगौ कलपदं गीतं शिवस्य मधुराक्षरम्।
श्रुत्वा स भगवान्प्रीतः शिवाविष्टो ननर्त ह॥१४॥

jagau kalapadaṁ gītaṁ śivasya madhurākṣaram|
śrutvā sa bhagavānprītaḥ śivāviṣṭo nanarta ha||14||

jagau — sang; kala-padam — sweet-toned; gitam — a song; shivasya — of Shiva; madhura-aksharam — with tender syllables; shrutva — hearing; sah — He; bhagavan — Bhagavan; pritah — pleased; shiva-avishtah — possessed by the mood of Shiva; nanarta — danced; ha — indeed.

14and sang a sweet-toned song of Shiva with tender syllables. Hearing it, Bhagavan was pleased and, possessed by the mood of Shiva, broke into dance.

Verse 15

तत उत्थाय तरसा गायनस्कन्धमारुहत्।
श्रीवासपण्डितस्तत्र शिवस्तोत्रं चकार ह।
महोक्षे स हरिस्तत्र वर्तुलाम्बुजलोचनः॥१५॥

tata utthāya tarasā gāyanaskandhamāruhat|
śrīvāsapaṇḍitastatra śivastotraṁ cakāra ha|
mahokṣe sa haristatra vartulāmbujalocanaḥ||15||

tatah — then; utthaya — rising; tarasa — swiftly; gayana-skandham — onto the singer's shoulders; aruhat — climbed; shrivasa-panditah — Srivasa Pandita; tatra — then; shiva-stotram — a hymn to Shiva; chakara — recited; ha — indeed; maha-ukshe — on the great bull; sah — He; harih — Hari; tatra — there; vartula-ambuja-lochanah — with round lotus eyes.

15Then He swiftly rose and climbed onto the singer's shoulders, and Srivasa Pandita recited a hymn to Shiva. And there, upon that great bull3, Hari, His lotus eyes grown round,

Verse 16

जटिलः शृङ्गडमरुवादको रामगायकः।
बभूव जगतां नाथः सर्वदेवमयो हरः॥१६॥

jaṭilaḥ śṛṅgaḍamaruvādako rāmagāyakaḥ|
babhūva jagatāṁ nāthaḥ sarvadevamayo haraḥ||16||

jatilah — with matted locks; shringa-damaru-vadakah — sounding the horn and the damaru drum; rama-gayakah — singing of Rama; babhuva — became; jagatam — of the worlds; nathah — the Lord; sarva-deva-mayah — containing all the gods; harah — Hara.

16became Hara4 — with matted locks, sounding the horn and the damaru, singing of Rama — the Lord of the worlds, containing all the gods within Him.

Verse 17

चक्रे महिम्नः स्तोत्रं स श्रीमुकुन्दोऽतिसुस्वरः।
अवरुह्य ततः स्कन्धाद्गायनस्याविशद्विभुः।
सर्वे ते मुदितास्तत्र हरिलीलारसप्लुताः॥१७॥

cakre mahimnaḥ stotraṁ sa śrīmukundo'tisusvaraḥ|
avaruhya tataḥ skandhādgāyanasyāviśadvibhuḥ|
sarve te muditāstatra harilīlārasaplutāḥ||17||

chakre — performed; mahimnah — "On the Greatness"; stotram — the hymn; sah — he; shri-mukundah — Sri Mukunda; ati-susvarah — with a most beautiful voice; avaruhya — descending; tatah — then; skandhat — from the shoulders; gayanasya — of the singer; avishat — sat down; vibhuh — the All-powerful; sarve — all; te — they; muditah — delighted; tatra — there; hari-lila-rasa-plutah — flooded with the rasa of Hari's pastimes.

17Sri Mukunda in a most beautiful voice performed the hymn "On the Greatness"5; then the All-powerful came down from the singer's shoulders and sat down. And all of them, flooded with the rasa of Hari's pastimes, rejoiced

Verse 18

कुर्वन्ति कीर्तनं हर्षात्तैः सहैव जगद्गुरुः।
गायन्रेमे हरेर्गीतं ननर्त च मुहुर्मुहुः॥१८॥

kurvanti kīrtanaṁ harṣāttaiḥ sahaiva jagadguruḥ|
gāyanreme harergītaṁ nanarta ca muhurmuhuḥ||18||

kurvanti — perform; kirtanam — kirtana; harshat — from joy; taih — with them; saha eva — together; jagat-guruh — the Teacher of the world; gayan — singing; reme — made merry; hareh — of Hari; gitam — song; nanarta — danced; cha — and; muhuh muhuh — again and again.

18and for joy perform kirtana; and the Teacher of the world made merry together with them, singing the song of Hari, and danced again and again —

Verse 19

श्रीमान्विश्वम्भरो देवो भक्तिभावसमन्वितः।
ततः परदिने नृत्यावसाने दण्डवत्क्षितौ॥१९॥

śrīmānviśvambharo devo bhaktibhāvasamanvitaḥ|
tataḥ paradine nṛtyāvasāne daṇḍavatkṣitau||19||

shriman — the glorious; vishvambharah — Vishvambhara; devah — the Lord; bhakti-bhava-samanvitah — filled with the feeling of devotion; tatah — then; para-dine — on the next day; nritya-avasane — at the end of the dance; danda-vat — like a rod; kshitau — on the ground.

19the glorious Lord Vishvambhara, filled with the feeling of devotion. And on the next day, when the dancing was over, He fell to the ground like a rod,

Verse 20

निपत्य संस्थितस्यास्य देवस्य पदपङ्कजात्॥२०॥

nipatya saṁsthitasyāsya devasya padapaṅkajāt||20||

nipatya — having fallen; samsthitasya — as He lay; asya — this; devasya — Lord; pada-pankajat — from the lotus feet.

20and as the Lord lay so, from His lotus feet

Verse 21

आगत्य ब्राह्मणी काचिज्जगृहे रज उत्तमम्।
तत उत्थाय भगवाञ्ज्ञात्वा तस्या विचेष्टितम्॥२१॥

āgatya brāhmaṇī kācijjagṛhe raja uttamam|
tata utthāya bhagavāñjñātvā tasyā viceṣṭitam||21||

agatya — approaching; brahmani — a brahmana woman; kachit — certain; jagrihe — took; rajah — the dust; uttamam — precious; tatah — then; utthaya — rising; bhagavan — Bhagavan; jnatva — learning; tasyah — her; vicheshtitam — deed.

21a certain brahmana woman came and took the precious dust. Then Bhagavan rose and, learning of her deed,

Verse 22

दुःखेन महताविष्टोऽनुतापी बहुधाभवत्।
तत उत्थाय सहसा वेगेन जाह्नवीजले॥२२॥

duḥkhena mahatāviṣṭo'nutāpī bahudhābhavat|
tata utthāya sahasā vegena jāhnavījale||22||

duhkhena — by sorrow; mahata — great; avishtah — overcome; anutapi — remorseful; bahudha — in many ways; abhavat — became; tatah — then; utthaya — springing up; sahasa — suddenly; vegena — swiftly; jahnavi-jale — into the waters of the Jahnavi.

22overcome by great sorrow, was full of remorse in every way6. Then He suddenly sprang up and swiftly

Verse 23

पपात मग्नस्तत्रैव तं दधार महाबलः।
अवधूतो महाबाहुर्धृत्वा तीरं समारुहत्॥२३॥

papāta magnastatraiva taṁ dadhāra mahābalaḥ|
avadhūto mahābāhurdhṛtvā tīraṁ samāruhat||23||

papata — threw Himself; magnah — sinking; tatra eva — right there; tam — Him; dadhara — caught hold of; maha-balah — the mighty; avadhutah — Avadhuta; maha-bahuh — mighty-armed; dhritva — holding; tiram — onto the bank; samaruhat — climbed.

23threw Himself into the waters of the Jahnavi and sank. But right there the mighty Avadhuta caught hold of Him; holding Him fast, the mighty-armed one climbed out with Him onto the bank.

Verse 24

श्रीवासहरिदासाद्या आगत्य त्राससंयुताः।
उद्विग्नाः सहसा वव्रुस्तं देवेशं भयान्विताः॥२४॥

śrīvāsaharidāsādyā āgatya trāsasaṁyutāḥ|
udvignāḥ sahasā vavrustaṁ deveśaṁ bhayānvitāḥ||24||

shrivasa-haridasa-adyah — Srivasa, Haridasa and others; agatya — having come; trasa-samyutah — terrified; udvignah — distressed; sahasa — at once; vavruh — surrounded; tam — that; deva-isham — Lord of the gods; bhaya-anvitah — full of fear.

24Srivasa, Haridasa and others came running, terrified and distressed, and, full of fear, at once surrounded the Lord of the gods.

Verse 25

प्रेमोत्कण्ठाश्च रुरुदुः शुक्लाम्बरद्विजादयः।
सुशान्तं सुखिनं ज्ञात्वा चक्रुः कृष्णकथां मिथः॥२५॥

premotkaṇṭhāśca ruruduḥ śuklāmbaradvijādayaḥ|
suśāntaṁ sukhinaṁ jñātvā cakruḥ kṛṣṇakathāṁ mithaḥ||25||

prema-utkanthah — yearning with love; cha — and; ruruduh — wept; shuklambara-dvija-adayah — the brahmana Shuklambara and others; su-shantam — fully calmed; sukhinam — happy; jnatva — knowing (Him); chakruh — held; krishna-katham — talk of Krishna; mithah — among themselves.

25The brahmana Shuklambara and others, yearning with love, wept; but, knowing that the Lord was fully calmed and happy, they began to speak of Krishna among themselves.

Thus ends the eleventh sarga, "The Plunge into the Jahnavi" (Jahnavi-patana), of the second prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. The Vishnu-sahasranama ("Thousand Names of Vishnu") from the Mahabharata or a similar hymn recited at rites.
  2. Nrisimha (Narasimha, Nrihari) is the Man-lion, the incarnation of Vishnu who tore apart the demon Hiranyakashipu for the sake of His devotee Prahlada.
  3. The singer on whose shoulders the Lord sits is likened to Nandin, the bull on which Shiva rides.
  4. Hara is Shiva. The horn, the damaru drum and the matted locks are his marks; Shiva is the greatest devotee of Rama, ever repeating His name. The Lord, who contains all the gods within Him, here displays the mood of Shiva, His greatest devotee; this does not make Shiva equal to Vishnu.
  5. The Shiva-mahimna-stotra ("Hymn on the Greatness of Shiva"), ascribed to Pushpadanta. Mukunda is Mukunda Datta, the singer among the Lord's companions.
  6. Taking the dust of someone's feet is a sign of worship, as before the Lord or a saint. The Lord, playing the part of a devotee, held Himself unworthy of such honour, and the woman's deed filled Him with remorse.
